skill.name: docker-workflow
skill.description: Docker workflow guidance for creating container images, Compose stacks, optimization plans, and debugging routines.
skill.summary: Create and troubleshoot Dockerfiles, Compose environments, and production container workflows.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most high-severity static hits are documentation false positives: Markdown fences, localhost health checks, apt cache cleanup, and Docker template braces. I confirmed real risk in hard-coded sample secrets, exposed SMTP/network behavior, an executable Docker helper, and semantic issues around credentials, environment dumps, backups, and cleanup. No evidence found of prompt injection text in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Hard-coded sample credentials and disabled service security appear in the Compose example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace defaults with placeholders, require secret files or environment injection, and keep admin services behind local profiles.

remediation.issue: The helper script can print all container environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the env command by default, redact sensitive names, or require an explicit unsafe flag before showing values.

remediation.issue: Cleanup commands force-prune Docker containers, images, volumes, and networks.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run mode, show planned deletions, and require confirmation before volume or network pruning.

remediation.issue: The backup command can export mounted application data to the host.
remediation.suggestion: Document sensitive data handling, restrict default destinations, and add warnings before archiving production volumes.

remediation.issue: The network helper pings a public resolver for connectivity checks.
remediation.suggestion: Make the probe endpoint configurable and default to an internal service or user-approved target.

semantic_findings.title: Hard-Coded Default Credentials in Compose Example
semantic_findings.description: The compose example uses default passwords such as postgres/password and admin/admin, and disables Elasticsearch security. Users may copy these defaults into reachable services.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced lines contain explicit default user names, passwords, and a disabled security setting. This is template content, but the risk is clear if copied into real deployments.

semantic_findings.title: Container Environment Dump Can Reveal Secrets
semantic_findings.description: The helper script prints every environment variable from a running container. This can expose database URLs, tokens, service passwords, and runtime secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The env command directly executes inside the chosen container and sorts all variables for display. Container environments commonly hold credentials and tokens.

semantic_findings.title: Forced Docker Cleanup Can Remove Local Data
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup workflow prunes stopped containers, images, volumes, and networks with force flags. Running it on the wrong host can remove local data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper uses Docker prune commands with -f and includes volume pruning. The README and skill also present broad cleanup commands without a dry-run step.

semantic_findings.title: Volume Backup Can Export Sensitive Data
semantic_findings.description: The backup command archives all container mounts to a caller-supplied destination. It can export database files, uploads, or secrets from running services.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The function enumerates mounts and writes tar archives to a host destination. This is legitimate administration, but it can copy sensitive application data.

content.value_statement: Container projects often need repeatable Dockerfiles, compose files, health checks, and debugging workflows. This skill gives structured Docker guidance, examples, and helper workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides multi-stage Dockerfile creation for Node.js, Python, Go, Java, and Rust projects.
Explains Docker Compose patterns for frontend, backend, database, cache, queue, and monitoring services.
Provides image optimization steps for layer caching, BuildKit, smaller base images, and dependency separation.
Documents container debugging workflows for logs, health checks, networks, ports, processes, and shell access.
Includes a Bash helper script for common Docker inspection, cleanup, backup, and optimization tasks.
limitations: The examples are templates and require project-specific review before production use.
The helper script acts on the local Docker daemon and can affect real containers.
It does not replace container security scanning or registry policy enforcement.
Some sample credentials and development services must be changed before deployment.

use_cases.title: Containerize a Web Application
use_cases.description: Create a Dockerfile, compose stack, health checks, and development overrides for a new application.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Environments
use_cases.description: Build repeatable local services for databases, caches, queues, monitoring, and application dependencies.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Container Issues
use_cases.description: Inspect health, logs, ports, networks, image size, and running processes during incident review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Docker Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my application stack and propose a simple Docker workflow with build, run, and health check steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create Compose Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Docker Compose setup for my frontend, API, database, cache, and worker services. Include development and production notes.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an Existing Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my current Docker build approach and recommend specific changes for smaller images, faster rebuilds, and safer runtime defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Dockerfile and Compose workflow for production readiness. Focus on secrets, users, health checks, networking, observability, and rollback risk.

output_examples.input: A Node.js API needs a production image and local database.
output: A two-stage image plan with dependency caching and a non-root runtime user.
A Compose service layout for the API, PostgreSQL, networks, volumes, and health checks.
A short production checklist for secrets, image tags, and restart policy review.

output_examples.input: A Docker image is too large and rebuilds are slow.
output: A layer ordering review that separates dependency installation from source changes.
Recommendations for slimmer base images, BuildKit cache mounts, and build context exclusions.
A validation plan using image history, size checks, and repeat build timing.

output_examples.input: A container is unhealthy after deployment.
output: A troubleshooting path covering logs, health check output, ports, networks, and resource limits.
Likely failure causes grouped by startup command, dependencies, permissions, and service discovery.
Follow-up checks for environment values, mounted volumes, and application readiness endpoints.

best_practices: Review every generated Docker command before running it on a shared or production host.
Replace all sample credentials with secret management before exposing services.
Pin base images and scan built images before promotion.
anti_patterns: Copying example Compose files into production without changing credentials.
Running cleanup commands on a host without checking volumes and stopped containers.
Publishing database, admin, or monitoring ports without access controls.

faq.question: Can this skill create Dockerfiles from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides Dockerfile structure, build stages, runtime user guidance, and optimization recommendations.

faq.question: Does it support Docker Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers multi-service Compose stacks, networks, volumes, health checks, and environment-specific overrides.

faq.question: Is it safe to run the helper script automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review each command first because the script can inspect containers, open shells, prune resources, and export volumes.

faq.question: Can I use the examples in production?
faq.answer: Use them as templates only. Change credentials, restrict exposed services, pin image versions, and run security scans first.

faq.question: Does it replace container security tools?
faq.answer: No. It supports workflow design, but you still need vulnerability scanning, policy checks, and secret management.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
